name: Chrome DevTools MCP
what: Lets a coding agent control and inspect a live Chrome browser through Chrome DevTools (Google now calls it "Chrome DevTools for agents"; the package is chrome-devtools-mcp). It can record performance traces, read network requests and console messages (with source-mapped stack traces) and automate pages with Puppeteer. A CLI is included for use without MCP. Apache-2.0.
who: Web developers who want the agent to debug a page or check its performance in a real Chrome.

setup.text: Needs a current Node.js LTS and Chrome stable (or Chrome for Testing).
Add to your MCP client config:
For basic browser tasks only, add "--slim" (and "--headless") to the args.

Google collects usage statistics by default; add "--no-usage-statistics" to opt out. Performance tools may send trace URLs to the CrUX API; "--no-performance-crux" turns that off. The agent can see everything in that browser, so don't use it with sensitive logged-in sessions.
Test it with the README's first prompt:

prompts: Check the performance of http://localhost:3000 and tell me the biggest issues.
Open my app, click Sign up, and show me any console errors or failed network requests.
Record a trace of the homepage load and explain what is slowing down LCP.
